title: Dangling Pointers
concept: If you keep holding the returned address card (pointer), you will get into trouble.

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
This is the standard input/output header.

This lesson addresses the problem of dangling pointers that keep pointing to freed memory.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created, and the allocation -> deallocation -> safety processing flow is checked.

steps.title: Heap memory allocation
steps.explanation: Allocate space for one integer in the heap and store its address in pointer `p`.

steps.title: Memory release and dangling pointers occur
steps.explanation:
After `free(p)`, the heap block is freed, but the `p` value remains and is in a dangling state.

Dereferencing this pointer will result in Undefined Behavior.

steps.title: Prevent dangling pointers (solution)
steps.explanation:
Reduce the risk of reuse by invalidating pointers with `p = NULL;`.

Assigning NULL immediately after release is the most basic defensive habit.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Key point: After freeing, the pointer is immediately cleared to NULL.

quiz.question: What is a Dangling Pointer?
quiz.explanation:
It means dangle.
It refers to a pointer that has no place to go.

misconceptions.wrong: When you free(p), p automatically becomes NULL.
misconceptions.correct: The C language is not that friendly.
misconceptions.why: Directly specifying `p = NULL;` is a C language programmer's manners and survival skill.

keyTakeaway: After saying `free`, tear up the receipt (`p`) in your hand (`NULL`).
